newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka gives rulers mandate to get on with work.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka gives rulers mandate to get on with work.

text.p: A victory in local elections has strengthened the hand of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government and it should now focus on Sri Lanka's chronic political and economic woes, newspapers and analysts said on Sunday.
Kumaratunga's People's Alliance (PA) scored a landslide triumph in Friday's local government polls, winning 194 of the 238 councils at stake.
The main opposition United National Party (UNP) could muster only 43 councils in violence-marred polls that were seen as a mid-term assessment of Kumaratunga's two and a half years of rule.

"With the stunning victory that the PA has secured, its hands have now been strengthened by the people to steer the nation out of crisis situation with confidence," the independent Island newspaper said.

It said the govenrment needed to tackle the war with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in the island's north and east and strengthen the economy of a country where millions still live below the poverty line.
The economic and human cost of the 13-year-old war with the LTTE rebels demanding a separate homeland has been huge for Sri Lanka.

The island has been spending some five percent of its gross domestic product in recent years to fight the war, which the government says has claimed more than 50,000 lives. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
Inflation is at nearly 17 percent and prices of food, fuel and services have risen as the war escalated after Kumaratunga became president in 1994 promising peace to her people.

"The steamroller majority that people accorded to the two-and-a-half year old government at the local polls is further binding on the government and it will have to harness all resources at its disposal to uplift the living conditions of the people," the Island said.

"The results are very encouraging as they indicate the total confidence people have placed in the leadership of the President with regard to the issues of war, political procedure, the economy...," Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister G.L. Peiris said.
Sri Lanka is in the midst of introducing constitutional reforms aimed at ending the ethnic war and granting wide autonomy to minorities. Peiris is widely seen as the architect of the peace plan.

The devolution package is currently with a select committee and is expected to be presented to parliament before November. If approved by two thirds of the deputies -- which will be difficult to achieve without UNP support -- it will be placed before the people in a referendum.
A Western diplomat said the PA was likely to use its latest victory to pressure the UNP into helping push the package through parliament.
"This is a strong possibility, as the PA will consider its win as a mandate for its peace package," the diplomat said.
